note: Drafted by the Opus 5 implementer from the 431 distinct quoted terms in tests/fixtures/boolean_corpus/ml_runs_76.json; Sam reviews every item carrying "unsure": true. Deliberate omissions: employers and research-lab names, conference names, single-surface tool/benchmark/dataset names (a named artifact earns a concept only when it has a real second surface form), and NOT-list exclusion vocabulary such as annotator or data labeling. Hyphen/space twins are never declared as separate forms - that axis is derived, so "post-training" implies "post training". Plural twins ARE declared when the corpus writes both, and are repeated in morphology only for common nouns. Every concept declares one or more families; a family is what lets a group reach across INTERRELATED concepts without reading as a grab-bag, and a concept that genuinely belongs to two neighbourhoods declares both, and related families sit under a shared parent in family_parents. Every concept also declares whether it names a CLASS of thing (a title, "LLM", "evaluation") or an INSTANCE of one (RLHF, SWE-bench); only a group of class concepts sharing a family can anchor a string. Named artifacts earn an instance concept even with one surface form, so that a sweep of benchmarks, frameworks, datasets, model names or venues is something the scorer can see; employers, labs and exclusion vocabulary stay out. The families venues and model_names are deliberately empty: a conference or a model name with one surface form earns no concept, so none of them is in here.
